item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Goddamn. As I've worked my way down the EoD hub I've seen points from the beginning of the 'verse through to millenia on from it, but fewer that are lower down in the economic scale or that deal with the consequences of anomalies having fewer checks on them. This piece reminds me (as I suppose it's meant to) of "ii tab po c h2o qhs prn pain" from Season One, but the horror goes even deeper into the eternal spiral of class hierarchies that sprouts when even the topmost levels are in a state of poorly regulated anarcho-capitalism.

(With editing, I could definitely see this as a solid piece of social commentary/allegory if you're still fond of it.)

item.content:encoded:
I had some difficulty envisioning the "hole" in the first few paragraphs and understanding the upside-down, sorta-figurative comparison that was being made by the narrator; I had to read that stuff twice. That said, once I did get it, it was effective and instantly immersive.

The first, more political half of this felt so real that I forgot the Foundationverse context entirely for a bit; it felt raw and societal and I took it at face value like I was reading it on the news. Thus, this is the second article on the wiki to make me cry this year. The second half of this (and the part about what happens to people who decay to the point of would-be-death) was just grotesque horror that I hate thinking about the implications of, so yeah, good work on all fronts. This is gut-twisting.

Nitpick: tenses of the italicized parts don't seem to match up:

As long as a steady supply of workers get emerging to go to work, they could not care less what happened within.

item.content:encoded:
Imagine, if you will, that you didn't read this.

Imagine that you've been spared the horror, that you were able to go about your day without being exposed to something so viscerally dark and unabashedly cruel.

Imagine that you found yourself reading something cute and lighthearted, something that makes you smile and laugh. Then, you may imagine your day brightened, not having read something so damnably uncomfortable.

I'd imagine you'd merely be missing out on some excellent writing. +1

Minor nitpick, if not already fixed by now.
>>>

She eats, she sleep, she fights

Wouldn't it be "sleeps" to match with the "s" of each verb fragment?

These are people are allowed

I think its "These people are allowed…" without the extra are.

a an easy and cost-effective source of bodies.

Don't believe "a" is necessary.


Phenomenal piece and I absolutely adore the usage of Kowloon in this sci-fi, dystopian variation on EoD canon. Described in such a way.

There's a loose narration that doesn't need to be confined to a clinical format or preset character. Its like from the mouth of a storyteller as she/he tells about the land and adds little characterizations to it.

Like for example: "Where do the brains come from? Why, mostly from genetically grown clone-stock, of course. No, we can't disclose any information about the process, or our facility."

Flows freely as we're prefaced with "Imagine…" at every beginning. First-person narration from the POV of the very company in contrast to the third-person on the enforcer.

I like that you made this doable. Maybe that's just me, but it's definitely hard to do for me. Thank you for this piece. +1.
